analysis: Examined the SandboxSetupCommand.swift change (head lines 11-15, 164-166, 185, 279-296). The PR adds a waitlist approval gate to the fresh-setup path only: `requireApproval()` (head 290-296) runs `FeatureWaitlistGate(...).require()` before `checkMac()` and the installer download/run, using a new injectable `waitlist: FeatureWaitlistAccess = .live()` property (head 166). The remainder is help text. Security impact: it adds a restrictive pre-check, so installer download and execution (TB-013 / T-061) is only reachable after the gate passes. It does not widen the installer trust boundary, the installer URL validation, or the execution path. The `.rerun` and `.alreadySetUp` branches (head 174-183) do not call the gate. They apply to Macs where the add-on is already installed or partly set up, so this is arguably intended, but the gate is not a security control on those paths. It is a product-access gate, and the add-on and coordinator presumably enforce enrollment approval server-side. The unchanged `.fresh` branch can be reached with `--yes`; `joinWithoutAsking: confirmed` auto-joins the waitlist under `--yes`. That is an account-side effect and low risk, and the user passed --yes explicitly. Unverified, since the sources were not supplied: FeatureWaitlistGate and FeatureWaitlistAccess.live() (network endpoints, auth token handling, TLS and failure behavior: fail-open vs fail-closed when the coordinator is unreachable, and whether provider API tokens A-008 are sent only to the coordinator origin). The next pass should check those, since the gate is a new client of the coordinator carrying credentials. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied diff. No threat-model IDs (TB-013, T-061) are weakened by this change.
